A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPEAR-1/SPEAR-VLM research. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A.1–A.4 are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original SIMPLER simulation experiments, real-world WidowX and Franka evaluations, and ablations in Tables 1–3, Figures 4–5, and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds a no-MoGe ablation result in Table 1.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline, objectives, and inference procedures are retained. Appendix A.1.2 replaces concatenation with averaging separately projected encoder features, matching Section 3.1 already in v1. This resolves a documentation inconsistency rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Training datasets, robot embodiments, and evaluation tasks remain unchanged. The added no-MoGe configuration uses the existing Bridge V2 subset and SIMPLER WidowX tasks, without extending dataset or scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds an evaluated comparator: PaliGemma pretrained on object-level 3D tasks without MoGe. The existing ablation comparators and benchmark comparisons with OpenVLA, SpatialVLA, π0-FAST, and π0.5 remain.

E3.justification: The experimental design gains a no-MoGe control, with SigLIP frozen during VLM pretraining and trainable during VLA training. Existing data subsets, training budgets, evaluation metrics, and real-world testing protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Table 1 ablation examines object-level 3D pretraining without the depth encoder. Earlier prompt, encoder-training, resolution, normalization, and rotation-formulation analyses are retained, including the appendix experiments.

E5.justification: Seed and deterministic-CUDA reporting, trial counts, and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. The new caption's description of improvement as 'not significant' is not accompanied by a statistical test or uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds no-MoGe success rates of 29.1%, 0%, 70.8%, and 4.1% across its four tasks, averaging 26.0%. Existing entries, including the 20.8% no-3D baseline and 35.4% full SPEAR-VLM average, are unchanged, as are other main-text and appendix results.

T1.justification: The flow-matching definitions, Equations 1–10, quaternion integration derivations, and tokenization mathematics are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about 3D pretraining, generalization, and matching or outperforming baselines using approximately 20 times fewer robot demonstrations. The additional ablation supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 now distinguishes gains from object-level training alone from the larger gains attributed to incorporating MoGe. Section 3.1 replaces the conjectured generalization advantage of affine-invariant depth with an unknown-camera-intrinsics rationale. Section 5 adds rotation estimation and collision detection as possible future priors; existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract adds spear.insait.ai as an access pointer for weights and annotated data. Appendix A.1.2 corrects the encoder-fusion description to separate projections followed by averaging. Hardware, training schedules, and data-processing instructions otherwise remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish a change in release status.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix A.4 are retained. Reference pagination and a small SpatialBot wording edit do not change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: There are localized wording edits, a revised ablation explanation, the corrected fusion description, and an added funding acknowledgment. The section organization and appendix structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a row and an expanded caption; Figures 4–5 are shortened vertically and surrounding content reflows. Table 1 introduces inconsistent numbering: two rows are labeled 3, while the final row remains labeled 5 despite references to row 6.

improvement.justification: V2 adds informative no-MoGe evidence, resolves the appendix/main-text conflict over encoder fusion, and supplies a resource-access pointer. These provide a limited net improvement. The new table has numbering errors, and the emphasized full-model versus no-MoGe comparison also changes SigLIP pretraining status, limiting its causal interpretation. Headline results remain unchanged.
